title: Findings inbox
summary: The ranked list of everything the detectors surfaced, and how to act on a row.

paragraphs: Detectors run after every sync and when you press Refresh findings. Rows are ordered by severity (Critical, Serious, Notable, Info), then confidence, then freshness. Severity glyphs pair a shape with text, so colour is never the only signal.

sections.heading: Filter, sort and load more
paragraphs: The inbox loads 50 findings at a time. When more exist it says so and offers Load 50 more. The severity buttons and the text box narrow only the findings already loaded, so a filter on a partial list is not a count of everything the detectors found. Sort switches between Ranked (the order above) and Newest first by last seen.

sections.heading: On each row
items: A basis chip says Legal claim: counted violation or Pattern signal, not a legal claim.
A confidence meter reads Unassessed or N% measured. Unassessed is not 0%.
Why we believe this opens the explanation and numbered citations: portal, document, character range and the quoted text. Open source document takes you to the source's records in Evidence.
Draft opens request or appeal drafts when the backend says a draft applies.
Dismiss removes a finding from the inbox and it stays dismissed. There is no undo control in the interface.

sections.heading: My organization
paragraphs: If you declared an organization and confirmed a match, the lens filters to findings about it. It never changes ranking, confidence, severity or any statutory result.

sections.heading: Routes that cannot be tested yet
paragraphs: Evidence gaps list checks the app could not run because the records are not collected yet, are not in the collected sources, or need a records request. A gap is not a finding and is not evidence of compliance.

sections.heading: Verifiable report
paragraphs: Under the list, Export a verifiable report writes one HTML file that checks its own signature in the reader's browser. Quoted text is masked for personal information, hypotheses about redacted identities are left out, and the file lists what was withheld. The signature shows the file is unchanged. It does not identify who holds the signing key.

title: Request and appeal drafts
summary: Drafts the app prepares. Nothing is sent.

paragraphs: A draft is plain text you edit, copy or download. The app has no email, portal or credential integration and never submits anything. You submit in the agency's own channel.

sections.heading: Where drafts come from
items: Findings inbox, Draft: Draft records request and, when it applies, Draft appeal or complaint. Availability is decided by the backend. If a finding names no specific gap, no draft applies. A pattern finding is not offered an appeal.

Evidence, statutory latency flag: Draft statutory deadline appeal. The backend refuses when the determination date is only a proxy or the extension record is defective, and shows the refusal as is. A separate Generate administrative appeal draft action saves a report and signed package to files on disk.

San Diego view, Plan an investigation or draft a request manually: pick a topic, choose dates, prepare an editable request draft, and download it. Open City request portal opens the agency site in your browser.

sections.heading: Reading a draft
items: Evidence basis says whether it rests on a pattern observation, a counted comparison against the agency's own stated commitment, or the statutory determination period.
Confidence is not assessed or a measured percentage.
Unknown to the app lists facts you must fill in before sending.
Citations and cited authorities are collapsible.
If you declared an affiliation, a locked Disclosure line is appended to every copy and download.

title: Reading a document
summary: The document dialog: masked text, provenance badge, audits and the verification log.

paragraphs: The viewer shows the local extracted text in chunks of 100,000 characters. Structured personal information such as identifiers is masked, and the header counts masked values. Detection is pattern based, so masking is best effort. Nothing in this dialog alters the original file.

sections.heading: Toolbar
items: Audit residual evidence: runs the collectors and reports Supported collector coverage complete or Coverage incomplete. An incomplete audit is not a negative finding.
Audit redactions: opens redaction tools (see Redaction tools).

Inspect revision history (PDF): reads earlier incremental saves. No earlier boundary does not rule out edits made before the file was created, and a boundary does not show that content was removed or concealed.
Verification log: every provenance check recorded for this document. An empty log is not a verification result.
Copy evidence link and Save excerpt to briefing.

sections.heading: Reference-only documents
paragraphs: When the original file is not stored, the first four actions are disabled and the badge reads Original referenced, file verification unavailable.

sections.heading: Annotations
items: Annotate opens a panel for notes, highlights and issue codes. Select text in the document, choose Use selected text, then save. A note can also be saved without a passage; it then belongs to the document as a whole and has no location.
An issue code needs a label you choose, such as amendment or missing attachment. Go to passage jumps to a saved mark that is in the chunk you are reading; marks in another chunk say so.
Copy as Markdown puts every annotation on this document on the clipboard with its character offset. Offsets locate text in the extracted copy, not the original file.
Annotations stay on this Mac in their own file and are not part of the record, a finding or any export. Deleting one asks for confirmation and cannot be undone.

sections.heading: Provenance badge
paragraphs: The badge reports one rung of the provenance ladder. See Provenance and C2PA. Quoted text drifted means the extracted text no longer hashes to the digest recorded at extraction, even if the file itself is intact.

title: Legal compliance panel and authority library
summary: Evaluate a request against a deadline rule and manage the authorities behind it.

paragraphs: In the Evidence view, the Legal compliance panel for a selected request evaluates it and lists active legal findings. Incomplete evidence sets are deferred rather than classified.

sections.heading: Recording an extension
paragraphs: Record notice stores what the agency claimed: when notice was given, the date it said it would respond by, the reason, and the source document. A request carries one extension and saving replaces it. Recording states what the agency claimed. Whether it moves the deadline is the evaluator's verdict on those dates. The app never fetches agency notices for you.

sections.heading: Findings
paragraphs: Each finding can show days overdue, missing evidence phrases, and a comparison of authority and evidence. You can confirm, dismiss or reopen a finding and save a reviewer note. Your review is a record of your judgment and does not change the computed result.

sections.heading: Authority library
paragraphs: Index statutes, ordinances or agency policies from a .md, .markdown or .txt file up to 8 MiB, or pasted text. Each gets a stable id, jurisdiction, citation, effective dates, an optional calendar-day deadline, and an official HTTPS address used as a label. Versions are content-addressed so you can compare text over time. Optional evidence rules match phrase sequences on word boundaries. Nothing is fetched from the address you enter.

title: Redaction tools
summary: Connect clues across records and scan a PDF for overlay problems.

sections.heading: Connect redacted clues across records
paragraphs: Compares public role holders, complementary number fragments, and unredacted versions of the same passage across retained text. Results are evidence-backed inferences and do not alter the original. Mask lengths stay unknown unless you confirm each block or X stands for exactly one character. Candidates contradicted by the constraints are marked.

sections.heading: PDF overlay integrity
paragraphs: A conservative scan of vector shapes, the text layer and metadata. A potential clash means approximate text bounds intersect a dark shape or redaction annotation. Backgrounds and layout elements can trigger this, and concealed content has not been established. Permanently removed content cannot be recovered. Review notes you write record geometry only, not recovered text.

title: Case workbench and casework
summary: Persistent local cases, ranked leads, signed exports and shared packets.

paragraphs: Open it from San Diego, Open casework and research tools. It needs the desktop app. Tabs: Cases and follow-through, Spending and outcomes, Coverage and changes, Evidence review, Usefulness. Above the tabs, a collapsed panel verifies signed packages.

sections.heading: Cases and follow-through
items: A case holds questions, hypotheses, falsification tests, records requests, productions, dated decisions and commitments. The app does not send requests. Dates and submissions are entered from your own records.
Ranked leads explain public consequence, available records, changed findings and dated decision opportunities. Scores prioritize review. They do not establish wrongdoing or confidence.
Contributor names are labels of responsibility, not authenticated identities.
Save case revision needs a contributor label. Exports use only the last saved revision.
Export signed chain-of-custody package writes a signed file. View export chain shows whether every link matches the prior export's hash. Withheld citations stay named, with a reason.
Review a shared case packet previews before applying and preserves conflicting local work.
Export signing key: a routine rotation keeps earlier packages trusted. Marking a key compromised cannot be undone, and packages signed by it are then untrusted.

title: Exports and package verification
summary: What the signed exports prove, and how to verify one.

paragraphs: Signed exports let a reader confirm a file is unchanged since signing. A signature shows integrity. It does not identify who holds the signing key or show that the contents are true.

sections.heading: Verify a package
paragraphs: Open a signed package (.json, up to 64 MB) in the verifier above the workbench tabs. The result is Overall: PASS, internally consistent and unaltered since signing, or Overall: FAIL, treat as unverified. Key status is reported separately: after a routine rotation earlier packages stay trusted. If the key was marked compromised, the signature can still be mathematically valid while the signer is no longer trusted, and the package should be treated as untrusted.

sections.heading: Exports in the app
items: Administrative appeal draft (Evidence): a report and a signed package on disk.
Case chain-of-custody package (Casework).
Verifiable report (Findings inbox): an HTML file that checks its own signature in the browser.

title: Evidence review and usefulness
summary: Challenge a saved investigation, record counterevidence, and assess usefulness.

paragraphs: Evidence review recomputes the quantities behind a saved investigation and lets you record a disposition, your reasoning and limits, what result would disprove the interpretation, and the counterevidence search you performed. Reviewer names are local attribution, not authenticated identities.

items: Public relationships are cited records with effective periods. A name match or documented connection does not establish misconduct.
Usefulness records a human assessment of whether an investigation helped, with time spent and an optional baseline. Without a baseline, time saved is not estimated.

paragraphs: A saved investigation is required. Autonomous research creates them.

title: Spending and outcomes
summary: Reconcile budget, actuals, encumbrances, contracts and outcomes for a fund.

paragraphs: This tab calculates over records you entered or imported: adopted funding history, spending, actual expenditures, open encumbrances, executed contracts and amendments, service outcomes, an account crosswalk and fund restrictions. Results are calculations. They do not establish program effectiveness or misconduct. Keep fiscal years, funds, budget cycles, populations and denominators separate before comparing.

title: Coverage and changes
summary: Acquisition priorities, publication changes and service access.

paragraphs: Coverage and changes turns unresolved questions into acquisition work. You define a consequential missing record, record its receipt after checking scope and period, and can reopen a gap. Publication changes compare a previously retrieved version with a subsequently retrieved one. Changes are review leads. A failed fetch is never treated as deletion. It works on local ingested records only.

title: Data upkeep and storage
summary: Scheduled rechecks, storage budget and retention.

paragraphs: Under San Diego, Collection, coverage and storage, you choose whether upkeep runs automatically, whether acquired tables are imported, whether sources are rechecked (every 6 hours, daily or weekly), a managed-file budget, and whether to keep original files with derived data or keep only references and extracted text. Recheck fetches the public sources you added. Recent upkeep activity is listed below the settings.

title: Check figures in a document
summary: Compares dollar figures and balance statements in one document with the tables you imported.

paragraphs: Check figures, in the document viewer, reads the document's masked text, extracts figures it can tie to a scope, and compares each with the imported financial tables. Each result is consistent, a mismatch showing claimed against observed with the query ids behind it, or not checkable.

sections.heading: Limits
paragraphs: A mismatch says the stated figure differs from the imported rows, not why. Text beyond the first 250,000 characters or more than 300 claims is skipped and reported as truncated. A check sees only what you imported.

title: Lead dossier
summary: Assembles one finding with its evidence chain, related findings, a falsification test and the gaps in the record.

paragraphs: A dossier gathers the cited evidence for one finding, other findings that share its subject, what would disprove it, and what the record does not contain. Each list reports when it was truncated.

sections.heading: Limits
paragraphs: A dossier organizes recorded facts. It does not establish cause, intent or wrongdoing.

title: Facility coverage
summary: Count public restrooms and their recorded daily open hours per area you define.

paragraphs: Import an agency's facility list as a table in Analysis, then open Facility coverage, choose the table and map its columns: facility name, an address or latitude and longitude, daily open hours, and optionally an id and a category. When a category column is mapped, list the category values that mean a public restroom; otherwise every row is counted. Define each area yourself, either as a latitude/longitude box (edges included) or as a list of facility ids. Areas are never guessed and addresses are never geocoded.

For each area the table shows the number of public restrooms, how many have recorded daily hours, how many have hours that could not be read, how many have no hours recorded, the part of a 24-hour day in which at least one facility with recorded hours is open, and the time in which none of them is open. Only recorded hours enter that arithmetic. When no facility in an area has recorded hours, both time figures read "not recorded" rather than 0 or 24 hours. Facilities with unrecorded or unreadable hours may be open when none of the recorded ones are.

Hours are read as one daily schedule: ranges such as 06:00-22:00 or 6am-10pm, several ranges separated by commas, "24 hours", "24/7" and "Closed". A range ending at midnight ends at the end of the day, and a range such as 20:00-02:00 wraps past midnight. Weekday-specific schedules, "dawn to dusk" and a range whose start equals its end are counted as unreadable. This view describes the list. It is not a finding and does not establish that a commitment was broken.
